hooks.text: A four-kilometer mountain swept past Earth while tumbling completely out of control.
Why was a four-kilometer asteroid tumbling past Earth completely out of control?
A giant asteroid buzzed Earth, but it was tumbling instead of spinning.

title: The Tumbling Mountain That Buzzed Earth
description: In 2004, asteroid Toutatis swept past Earth closer than any object of its size this century, revealing a bizarre tumbling ginger root.

beats.text: A four-kilometer mountain swept past Earth while tumbling completely out of control.
beats.visual: Computer-generated radar model of asteroid 4179 Toutatis tumbling in space, 2004

beats.text: On September 29, 2004, the asteroid Toutatis made a startlingly close approach.
beats.visual: Telescope image of asteroid 4179 Toutatis passing background stars, 2004

beats.text: It swept within four lunar distances, or roughly 1.5 million kilometers of Earth.
beats.visual: Diagram showing asteroid Toutatis trajectory passing the Earth and Moon orbit, 2004

beats.text: Measuring roughly 4.5 kilometers in length, it was the closest flyby of its size this century.
beats.visual: Radar delay-Doppler image of asteroid 4179 Toutatis from Goldstone Observatory, 2004

beats.text: Online chain emails predicted doom, but radar dishes at Goldstone and Arecibo mapped its true face.
beats.visual: Photograph of the 70-meter Deep Space Network antenna at Goldstone Observatory, 2004
queries: Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex 70m antenna

beats.text: Toutatis was a contact binary of two distinct lobes, shaped remarkably like a ginger root.
beats.visual: Optical image of asteroid 4179 Toutatis captured by China's Chang'e 2 spacecraft, 2012

beats.text: Stranger still, it never spins cleanly, tumbling through space like a flubbed pass across two independent cycles.
beats.visual: Computer model showing the non-principal-axis rotation cycles of asteroid Toutatis, 2004

beats.text: Calculations prove Earth is safe for at least six centuries from that chaotic wanderer.
emphasis: safe for at least six centuries
beats.visual: Orbital diagram of asteroid 4179 Toutatis around the Sun and Earth, 2004

better_than_last: Eliminated secondary timeline subplots and academic designations to sustain pacing through the tumbling motion reveal.
